children: Better Home released preliminary, unaudited results for Q3 2026 showing Loan Volume of $1.395 billion and Total Net Revenues of $45.1 million. The company reported a preliminary net loss of $33.1–$34.1 million and a preliminary Adjusted EBITDA loss of $24.8–$25.8 million, which includes about $8.0 million of proxy-related expenses. Management noted the proxy contest weighed on conversion and partner launches but said loan volume remained within prior guidance.
Total Net Revenues: $45.1 million (preliminary for Q3 2026).
Loan Volume: $1,395.0 million for Q3 2026 (preliminary), within prior guidance of $1,375M–$1,525M.
Net Loss (GAAP, preliminary): $(33.1) million to $(34.1) million for Q3 2026.
Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP, preliminary): $(24.8) million to $(25.8) million for Q3 2026; includes approximately $8.0 million of proxy-related legal, PR and other expenses.
Company expects a non-cash reversal of stock-based compensation of approximately $7.0–$8.0 million in Q3 2026 related to forfeiture of unvested equity awards.
Loan Volume increased 15.3% year over year but decreased 16.3% sequentially versus Q2 2026; revenue increased 8.6% year over year and decreased 17.5% sequentially.
Management attributed below-guidance revenue and slower partner launches to interest rate headwinds and a proxy solicitation that diverted resources and impacted morale and conversion.

Company reported strong liquidity: $81 million in cash and cash equivalents and $9 million in restricted cash, plus an unencumbered tangible equity position in the UK bank expected to generate additional proceeds upon anticipated sale.

Board goals highlighted: drive to Adjusted EBITDA breakeven on a go-forward basis (given current rates and planned savings), expedite sale of the Birmingham Bank, and transition to an AI-first operating model to materially lower per-loan production costs.
